subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR` and require users to move it or select an unused destination, while reclaiming only a checkout with matching updater-owned state and marker?
rationale: This is an intentional security-versus-upgrade-compatibility contract: source inspection and tests can establish implementation behavior, but cannot choose the user-facing policy for established package installs.

options.title: Approve fail-closed conversion
options.body: Accept the documented operator action so package installs never build from an adopted checkout, while verified updater-created interrupted checkouts remain reclaimable.

options.title: Preserve existing-path conversion
options.body: Require a different compatibility design that safely verifies or migrates established destinations instead of rejecting them outright.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed conversion
recommendation.body: Accept the documented operator action so package installs never build from an adopted checkout, while verified updater-created interrupted checkouts remain reclaimable.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion already identifies vincentkoc as the updater/configuration owner asked to approve this precise policy.
